cards: Akhenaten was an Egyptian pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty who reigned c. 1353–1336 BCE.
Amenhotep III was a pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt in the fourteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1390–1352 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ashur-uballit I was king of Assyria from 1365 to 1330 BCE.
Aziru was the ruler of Amurru in the fourteenth century BCE and the son of Abdi-Ashirta.
Abdi-Ashirta was the ruler of Amurru, a land in the mountains and coast of present-day northern Lebanon and western Syria, in the fourteenth century BCE.
Pan Geng was a king of the Shang dynasty of China, traditionally credited with moving the capital to Yin, near modern Anyang, around 1300 BCE.
fl. c. 1300 BCE · Central & East Asia
Napir-Asu was a queen of Elam in the fourteenth century BCE, wife of King Untash-Napirisha.
Tadukhipa was a Mitanni princess, daughter of King Tushratta, who was sent to Egypt with a rich dowry to marry the ageing Pharaoh Amenhotep III near the end of his reign.
fl. 14th century BCE · Ancient Near East
Thutmose IV was a pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt in the fourteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1400–1390 BCE · Ancient Near East
Abdi-Heba was the ruler of Jerusalem, called Urusalim, in the mid-14th century BCE, known from six of his letters to the Egyptian pharaoh among the Amarna letters.
Ammunira was the ruler of Beirut in the mid-14th century BCE, a vassal of the Egyptian pharaoh.
Biridiya was the ruler of Megiddo in Canaan in the fourteenth century BCE, a vassal of the Egyptian pharaohs.
Kurigalzu I was a Kassite king of Babylonia in the early 14th century BCE.
Labayu was ruler of Shechem in the hill country of Canaan in the mid-14th century BCE, known from the Amarna letters.
Merymose was viceroy of Kush, the 'King's Son of Kush', under Amenhotep III in the early 14th century BCE.
Tudhaliya I was a king of the Hittites, usually dated to the late 15th or early 14th century BCE, at the start of the period often called the Hittite New Kingdom.
c. 15th–14th century BCE · Ancient Near East
